slides.title: Iterators and Generators Overview
slides.prompt: An iterator is an object that contains a countable number of values and implements the iterator protocol (__iter__ and __next__). Generators are simple ways to create iterators using functions and the 'yield' keyword, providing memory-efficient lazy evaluation.
slides.codeSnippet:
# Generator Function
def count_up_to(max_val):
    count = 1
    while count <= max_val:
        yield count
        count += 1

counter = count_up_to(3)
print(next(counter))  # 1
print(next(counter))  # 2

slides.title: Yield From Expression
slides.prompt: What is the primary purpose of the 'yield from' expression in Python generators?
options: To delegate generator operation to a sub-generator or iterable
To return a value and permanently terminate the generator execution
To catch StopIteration exceptions automatically inside loops
To convert a generator into a standard list
slides.correctAnswer: To delegate generator operation to a sub-generator or iterable
